Maya Chen: heads up — hitting onboarding friction w/ the JS SDK imports. Quickstart shows `require('@redwood/inference')` but my Vercel Edge deploy fails with `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module`. Local Node 18 serverless works fine.

Samir Patel: what does your package.json look like? is `type` set to module?

Maya Chen: no, it's the default create-next-app one (no `type` field). Using TS, SDK @redwood/inference@2.1.0. stack: Next 13 edge function. Error trace: `Unexpected token 'export'` from node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.cjs maybe?

Alex R.: quick context: we ship both ESM and CJS builds but the exports map is a little confusing for people using edge runtimes. Edge requires ESM; `require(...)` pulls the CJS entry which sometimes references `export`-style code in the bundle.

Alex R.: short workaround: use ESM import in edge functions. e.g. in a Next edge handler do:

```js
// next edge -- module file
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference/edge';
// or if your setup resolves ESM by package exports
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
```

Maya Chen: we don't want to force customers to change project-wide `type: module`. Any CJS-friendly pattern?

Alex R.: for pure CJS Node (non-edge) you can do:

```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference').default || require('@redwood/inference');
```

But for Edge (Vercel) you need ESM. For TS consumers also watch `esModuleInterop`/`allowSyntheticDefaultImports` — types can look wrong if those compiler options are off.

Samir Patel: thanks — so doc suggestion: show three quick examples (CJS Node, ESM Node, Edge ESM) and a tiny TS note about `esModuleInterop`. Saves users poking around.

Maya Chen: +1. Also saw people confused about default vs named exports for `RedwoodClient` vs `createInference`. Example in quickstart shows a named import but the package exports default in some bundlers.

Kevin T.: FYI I opened a docs PR to add an "Import patterns" section and explicit Edge snippet, waiting review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 (WIP).

Maya Chen: awesome — can you also add a tiny troubleshooting blurb: "If you see Cannot use import statement outside a module, check runtime (Edge vs Node) and prefer ESM import for Edge" ?

Kevin T.: will do. Also adding a short note for TypeScript: either use `import Redwood from '...'` with `esModuleInterop: true` or `import * as Redwood from '...'` without it.

devx-bot: Docs PR 412 linked by Kevin T. moved to review queue. :eyes:

Samir Patel: bonus tip for sample apps — we should ship a minimal `edge` example folder (edge/handler.mjs) that folks can copy/paste. saves so many tickets.

Alex R.: agreed. I'll add an issue to track sample-app parity (edge + cjs + types).

Maya Chen: thanks all — unblocked for now using the ESM import in the edge function. I'll test the docs snippet once PR lands. :raised_hands:
